explanation: In Italian business culture, gift-giving is polite but must be modest and not appear as a bribe. High-quality items like wine, gourmet food, or elegant office accessories are appreciated, but expensive gifts can create discomfort or be seen as inappropriate.
local_tip: Present the gift without ostentation, and if it is wine or food, suggest it be shared with the team to avoid singling out the recipient.
regional_note: In Southern Italy, gifts may be more warmly received, while in the North (e.g., Milan, Turin) business relationships are more formal and gifts are less expected.

also_check.note: Gift-giving is highly ritualized; wrapping and presentation are crucial, and gifts are often exchanged at first meetings.
Gifts are rarely given in initial business meetings; a small token is acceptable only after a relationship is established.
Gifts are common, but avoid alcohol or items with pig imagery; use the right hand and respect Islamic customs.
